title: Plan the Home Grow Before Starting Plants

content.overview: A successful small grow starts with constraints, not equipment shopping. First determine whether cultivation is permitted where you live, then define household safety, privacy, available space, environmental control and time you can realistically maintain.

vocabulary.definition: A limit that shapes what a cultivation plan can safely or practically support.
The defined size, purpose and boundaries of a project.
A planned response to a foreseeable failure or interruption.

sections.title: Verify the rules that actually apply
sections.body: Cannabis and hemp requirements vary by location. Do not treat a national overview or another state's rules as authorization for a home project.

sections.title: Keep water, electricity and access in the plan
sections.body: Wet work, heat-producing equipment, cords and restricted access create household hazards. Use qualified equipment and do not defeat electrical or fire-safety protections.

sections.title: Start smaller than maximum capacity
sections.body: A small crop is easier to observe, water, train and correct while you learn the system.

workedExamples: A tent that physically fits six plants may be a poor plan if dehumidification, access or post-harvest space supports only two or three well.
Buying equipment before verifying local rules can create cost without a lawful use path.
commonMistakes: Using temporary household electrical arrangements as permanent infrastructure.
content.practicalApplication: Write one page listing legal verification source, maximum intended crop size, space, light/environment system, water access, safety controls and drying/storage plan.
content.summary: A home grow becomes manageable when its legal, safety and capacity limits are defined before plants begin.
